\section{A flag inside a texttt span}

The regression baseline is re-run with \texttt{--check}, and the fast pytest
subset is selected with \texttt{-m "not slow"}. Both spans are typeset in a
monospace face rather than as prose, so the double hyphen in the first one is
not a ligature and is left alone.

Nested braces have to survive too: \texttt{npu-opt --pass-pipeline="builtin.module(canonicalize)"}
is one span and the linter must not stop reading it at the first closing brace
it happens to find.

Everything outside those spans is ordinary prose and uses ASCII hyphens only,
as in out of tree, or in the phase name phase/p0-foundations.
